comparator.name: Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the current Dutch-language 'Bachelor Science, Business and Innovation' overview, 'Inhoud' (content) and 'Toekomst' (career) pages; the FAQ page; and the current 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations (OER), Article 11.3 of which states the full compulsory-unit table with vakcode, EC and niveau for every named unit. Article 10.2 (Afstudeerrichtingen) records 'n.v.t.': the normalized target cp-000116 (registry row 124, source_provider_id 111A136, recognized_programme_code 50670, languages_json=["NLD"]) is the generic Dutch-taught Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation with no formal afstudeerrichting to instantiate, so routeSelection is null. Article 11.3's Year 1 (60 EC): Veiligheid op het lab (AB_LABSAFETY, 0 EC) and Taaltoets NL (VU_TAALTOETS, 0 EC) carry no separate credit -- Article 10.4.5 folds the taaltoets into the grade of Innovatieproject energie, and Article 9.1 folds the lab-safety fire-extinguisher instruction and safety test into the completion gate of Practicum natuurkunde -- so neither is encoded as its own credited component; the 11 remaining Year-1 units (Waardegedreven innoveren onderzoeken en ondernemen + tutoraat XB_0165 6 EC, Science Entrepreneurship & Digital Innovation XB_0167 6 EC, Calculus X_400617 6 EC, Biochemie X_401109 6 EC, Innovatieproject geneesmiddelen X_435095 6 EC, Organic & Sustainable Chemistry XB_0168 6 EC, Lineaire algebra X_400302 3 EC, Van molecuul tot medicijn X_430581 3 EC, Ondernemerschap en Digitale Innovatie XB_0166 6 EC, Duurzame Energie XB_0169 6 EC, Innovatieproject energie X_420196 6 EC) sum to the required 60 EC. Year 2 (60 EC, Article 11.3): Strategic Management of Technology and Innovation E_MFEN_SMTI 6 EC, Finance I E_EBE1_FIN1 6 EC, Innovatieproject diagnostiek & gezondheid X_420225 6 EC, Innovatieproject energietransitie XB_0097 6 EC, Maatschappelijk verantwoord ondernemen en duurzaamheid X_420564 6 EC, Fysica: electriciteit en magnetisme X_430069 3 EC, Klinische diagnostiek en Imaging XB_42000 6 EC, Onderzoek ontwerp en methodologie XB_0188 6 EC, Toegepaste informatica & programmeren voor SBI XB_0186 6 EC, Klassieke mechanica & thermodynamica XB_0187 6 EC, Practicum natuurkunde X_420193 3 EC. The Overgangsbepalingen (Article 15.2, changes per 2026-2027) confirm X_420227 Toegepaste informatica (3 EC) is now folded into XB_0186 (6 EC) and X_430579 Thermodynamica (3 EC) into XB_0187 (6 EC), so the Article 9.1 prerequisite naming X_420227 for Modelleren is satisfied by XB_0186 for the 2026-2027 cohort. Year 3 (60 EC): Article 11.3 fixes Modelleren X_420519 3 EC, Wijsgerige vorming 2: wetenschapsfilosofie X_428002 3 EC (the current official overview page calls this unit 'Technology Assessment & Ethics in a Digital World'; the OER Article 11.3 table is the controlling source for the compulsory-unit table and is used here) and Bachelorproject SBI X_430509 24 EC (Article 9.1: admission requires at most 18 EC of the bachelor's other units outstanding and Onderzoek ontwerp en methodologie passed) as the 30-EC compulsory core, plus Article 12.1's genuine first-semester vrije keuzeruimte of at least 30 EC, filled by a minor, a free choice of units (at least 12 EC at level 300, at most 6 EC at level 100) or study abroad (Article 12.2 names two minors -- Educatieve minor Natuurkunde, Educatieve minor Scheikunde -- that need no examination-board approval). No target-specific evidence favours one minor, so -- consistent with Section 2.1's instruction to preserve genuine open elective or profiling space explicitly rather than inventing content for it -- this 30-EC space is recorded as a single generic keuzeruimte/minor component. 60 (Year 1) + 60 (Year 2) + 60 (Year 3: 30 compulsory core + 30 keuzeruimte/minor) = 180 EC. Article 10.3's beoogde leerresultaten independently corroborate this reconstruction, naming basic principles of physics, chemistry and pharmaceutical science, mathematics for describing physical/chemical/business processes, and business/organisational/entrepreneurship principles, 'welke verband houden met energie- en levenswetenschappen' (which relate to energy and life sciences) as the programme's own two named application domains -- independently corroborated by the current official Toekomst page's explicit 'Energy & Sustainability' and 'Life & Health' career tracks. No further official source needed to be consulted: the current official overview/content/career/FAQ pages and the 2026-2027 OER together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC and niveau for every compulsory unit, current confirmation of the 2026-2027 course-code transition for the informatics and thermodynamics units, and an explicit, UCR-independent judgment (preserving rather than instantiating the free keuzeruimte/minor) fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's generalist Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation (Article 10.2 confirms no formal afstudeerrichtingen exist for this normalized target): a business-and-innovation-methods core -- entrepreneurship, strategy, research methodology, econometrics, finance, mathematics, data science, programming, organisational psychology and philosophy of science/technology ethics -- applied evenly across UCR's sustainability/environment offerings and its biomedical/life-science offerings, reproducing as closely as UCR's catalogue allows the programme's own combination of exact-science literacy, business training and innovation-project work spanning both of its own named application domains, while leaving the 30-EC free keuzeruimte/minor honestly preserved as unclaimed elective space and the physics/chemistry components genuinely unmatched, since UCR offers neither discipline.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines UCR's business/entrepreneurship/finance cluster (7 of 24: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Research Methods & Statistics, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance, Introduction to Economics), a mathematics/data/programming cluster (4 of 24: Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science), an organisational-behaviour and ethics cluster (2 of 24: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Ethics), an energy/sustainability cluster (4 of 24: Sustainability Essentials I, Climate Change, Governance of Sustainability, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy) and a life-science/health cluster (5 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity), plus Dynamic Earth and Personal & Professional Development. The label names technology innovation management first for the dominant business/methods/strategy backbone that runs through every semester, and energy and life sciences second because the curriculum deliberately balances UCR's sustainability offerings against its biomedical/life-science offerings in roughly equal measure, reproducing the comparator's own parallel Year-1/Year-2 innovation-project structure (medicines and energy in Year 1; diagnostics/health and the energy transition in Year 2) and its own two published career tracks (Energy & Sustainability; Life & Health) rather than favouring either domain.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the two generator-eligible programme-interest rows that specifically name 'sustainable energy innovation' (a stable study direction, row 5287) and 'the energy transition for companies and governments' (a direct programme interest, row 5302) as recurring foci of the current programme, corroborated by the support row on alternative fuels (5303) and by the programme's own current official Toekomst page naming 'Energy & Sustainability' as one of its two published career tracks with an explicit Energy Science master's continuation: a concentration retaining the same shared business/methods/ethics core but replacing the closest match's life-science/health breadth with UCR's full available sustainability, environmental-governance and renewable-energy-systems offerings, studying how companies and governments manage the transition to sustainable energy.

The label names sustainable energy innovation first for the dominant, now much deeper sustainability-cluster content, and the energy transition second for the governance, renewable-system-design and resource-economics content that together organise this alternative's distinctive academic priorities.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: VU's Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation names 'sustainable energy innovation' and 'the energy transition for companies and governments' as two of its own generator-eligible programme-interest rows (5287, 5302), independently corroborated by the current official Toekomst page naming 'Energy & Sustainability' as one of only two published career tracks (alongside 'Life & Health') and by the programme's own OER learning outcomes naming 'energie- en levenswetenschappen' as its twin application domains. The closest match reproduces the shared business/methods/ethics core together with an even balance of UCR's sustainability and life-science offerings, standing in for the comparator's own parallel Year-1/Year-2 energy-and-health project structure. This alternative instead retains the identical shared business/methods/ethics core (14 of 24 courses) but replaces the closest match's five life-science/health courses with five new UCR sustainability/energy courses (Sustainability Essentials II, Renewable System Design, Earth's Resources, R3: Recycling Recovery Remediation, Earth Observation), for a total of nine energy/sustainability courses concentrating the programme on how technology and governance drive the energy transition. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a balanced dual-domain generalist programme to a single-domain energy concentration, and the two alternatives share 19 of 24 courses while differing in 5 of 24 each way (37.5 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different third UCR route evidenced by the generator-eligible programme-interest row that specifically names 'life-science and health innovation' (a stable study direction, row 5288) as a recurring focus of the current programme, corroborated by the support rows on chemistry/biochemistry/molecules-to-medicines (5294) and clinical diagnostics and imaging (5300), and by the programme's own current official Toekomst page naming 'Life & Health' as its other published career track: a concentration retaining the same shared business/methods/ethics core but replacing the closest match's energy/sustainability breadth with UCR's full available biomedical, life-science and health-psychology offerings, studying the biological and human dimensions of medical and health-technology innovation.

This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a balanced dual-domain generalist programme to a single-domain health/life-science concentration, and this alternative differs from the closest match in 5 of 24 courses each way (37.5 EC) and from the energy alternative in 10 of 24 courses each way (75 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum in both comparisons.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for HCBLIFE213, HCBBIOM311, HCBBIOM313 and HCBBIOM312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENENTR212 (semester 2), BENENTR311 and BENBUSI312 (semester 6), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 5) and BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally require it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISMATH211 (semester 3), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Programming, Sustainability Essentials I, Research Methods & Statistics) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (Pharmacology, Governance of Sustainability, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns ten generator-eligible rows: bringing sustainable and medical innovations to market (5283); combining science, business and innovation (5284); turning scientific knowledge into practical products (5285); evaluating the technical and commercial feasibility of innovation (5286); technology entrepreneurship (5289); technology and innovation strategy (5290); innovation projects for real organisations (5291); research, design and innovation methodology (5292); management and organisation (5298); and corporate social responsibility and sustainability (5299), all of which describe the programme's own general business-and-innovation-methods core rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate. The remaining three generator-eligible rows -- sustainable energy innovation (5287), life-science and health innovation (5288) and the energy transition for companies and governments (5302) -- were independently assessed as two coherent candidate directions, 'Sustainable Energy Innovation and the Energy Transition' (5287, 5302) and 'Life-Science and Health Innovation Management' (5288), additionally supported by curricular-topic evidence (alternative fuels, chemistry/biochemistry/molecules-to-medicines, clinical diagnostics and imaging) and independently corroborated by the programme's own current official Toekomst page naming exactly these two tracks -- Energy & Sustainability and Life & Health -- as its only published specialisations. Both candidates pass all four gates: each is evidence-backed by generator-eligible rows the programme's own current official sources independently corroborate as one of its two headline application domains; each has a clear organising logic (deepening one of the comparator's own two application domains while retaining the shared business/methods/ethics core); each is substantively distinct, replacing at least 5 of the closest match's 24 courses (at least 37.5 EC) with UCR's own deeper sustainability or biomedical/life-science offerings, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and each is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with at least six distinct level-300 courses and pairwise differences of at least 5 courses (37.5 EC) against the closest match and 10 courses (75 EC) against each other, comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes both as the second and third alternatives. No generator-eligible evidence remains unassigned after the closest match and these two candidates together account for all thirteen generator-eligible rows, so production includes the maximum of three alternatives and records 'maximum-reached' as the stopping state.

notes.text: VU's Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation combines a continuous beta-science core (physics, chemistry, mathematics) with business, entrepreneurship and innovation-management training, applied to two parallel domains, energy and life sciences. At UCR, students can approach most of this same business/innovation territory through UCR's business, entrepreneurship, finance, data-science and programming courses, and can approach the programme's own energy and life-science application domains through UCR's environment-and-sustainability and health/biomedical-science offerings, but UCR does not teach physics or chemistry as a discipline at any level, so it does not reproduce the comparator's own beta-science core. These pathways therefore compare related applied fields; UCR's programmes approach the comparator's subject matter through UCR's own combination of disciplines rather than reproducing the external beta-science-and-business curriculum course by course.

All three UCR alternatives include substantial study of the comparator's shared business, entrepreneurship and innovation-methods core. The comparator additionally includes specialist beta-science components -- organic and sustainable chemistry, classical mechanics and thermodynamics, electricity and magnetism, and a dedicated physics laboratory practicum -- that UCR does not offer at any level of depth; UCR students can instead combine adjacent environment/sustainability or biomedical/life-science coursework, but those specialist physics and chemistry components are not offered at the same level of depth or in dedicated form.
